title: Caldo Verde
subtitle: Portuguese kale and potato soup with chorizo
excerpt: Portugal's national soup: a broth of blended potato and onion scattered with ribbons of dark kale and slices of chouriço. Simple, deeply satisfying, and made in under 30 minutes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Caldo verde (literally 'green broth') is Portugal's most beloved soup, originating in the Minho region of northern Portugal and now eaten as a national dish at family meals, celebrations, and restaurants across the country. The soup has a simple base of potato and onion blended into a smooth broth, into which very finely shredded dark kale (or Portuguese couve-galega) is added raw in the last few minutes of cooking so it retains its colour and slight texture. Chouriço or chorizo adds a smoky, paprika note. The kale must be sliced as finely as possible into thread-like ribbons; this is the defining visual characteristic. The soup is finished with a generous drizzle of olive oil.

content.text: The kale must be cut into the finest possible ribbons; remove the tough central rib first and stack several leaves before rolling them tightly and slicing crossways as thin as you can. Add the kale only in the last 3 to 4 minutes of cooking so it stays bright green rather than turning khaki.

items.preparation: ribs removed; very finely shredded into thread-like ribbons

content.text: Fry the chorizo slices in the olive oil for 2 minutes until lightly browned. Remove and set aside. Add the onion and garlic to the same pot and cook for 5 minutes. Add the potato and stock. Bring to a boil and simmer for 20 minutes until the potato is very tender.
Blend the soup until completely smooth with a stick blender. Season well. Return to a simmer.

Add the shredded kale to the soup and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until just tender and still bright green. Add the chorizo slices. Ladle into warm bowls, drizzle with olive oil, and serve with crusty bread.
